chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Aban, from Abu al-Hurr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man came to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said, 'I gifted a slave girl to the Ka'bah, and I was given five hundred dinars for her. So what is your view?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Sell her, then take her price, then stand upon the wall of the Hawd (Basin of the Ka'bah), then call out and give to everyone who has been cut off (by bandits or circumstances) and every needy one among the pilgrims.'

key_terms.الْكَعْبَةِ: The Ka'bah, the sacred house in Mecca
key_terms.حَائِطِ الْحِجْرِ: The wall of the Hijr (Hijr Ismail), a semi-circular wall adjacent to the Ka'bah
key_terms.دِينَارٍ: Dinar, a gold coin used as currency
key_terms.مُنْقَطَعٍ: One who is cut off or stranded

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a slave girl gifted to the Ka'bah?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the practical application of 'gifted to the Ka'bah' (muqaddama), where the slave girl was not permanently endowed but rather held in trust for the benefit of pilgrims. The Imam’s directive to sell her and distribute the proceeds to stranded pilgrims (muqtarid) highlights the charitable purpose of such endowments in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing it from permanent waqf. This reflects the broader Shia understanding that gifts to the Ka'bah often serve as a mechanism for supporting the spiritual and material needs of the hajj community.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Salih Bin Al Sandy, from Ja’far Bin Basheer, from ban, from Abu Al Hurr, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A man came over to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, so he said, ‘I have gifted a slave girl to the Kabah, and I have given five hundred Dinar for her. So what is your<sup>asws</sup> view?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Sell her. Then take her price, then stand upon the wall of the (Black) Stone. Then call out, and give to everyone who has been cut off (by bandits), and every needy one, from the Pilgrims’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Salih al-Sindiy from Ja’far ibn Bashir from Aban from abu al-Hurr who has said the following:

“Once, a man came to abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘I have given a slave-girl as a gift to al- Ka‘bah and I had paid for her five hundred. What is your instruction? He (the Imam) said, ‘Sell the slave-girl, and with whatever amount you will receive from the sale go to the wall near the Black Stone, make an announcement and give to those looted on the way and to every needy of the people performing Hajj.’”
